The public job page is a separate Flask template, not the panel. Next I’ll check how that career-page link is gated versus the 3-jobs-per-day rule.

The career-page link is doing two separate things, and both are working as currently coded — they just fight the older product rule. **The layout looks off because this page is a second, simpler UI.** `/jobs/mollie-senior-platform-engineer` is not the Next homepage. It is a Flask interstitial (`job_posting.html` + `job-posting.css`) built for LinkedIn wrapping. The header is a stripped copy of marketing chrome, and the employer link was never styled as a real secondary button. **The direct Mollie link is an explicit leak around the 3-a-day wall.** Signed-in users always get “Continue to the official … career page.” The 3-free-jobs limit only gates *saving into Kuchup*, not leaving to the ATS. That contradicts the panel policy you already decided. --- ### Why the UI looks different Marketing pages (`/`, `/pricing`, `/how-it-works`) use the Next header: glass nav, BrandLockup, Product / Countries / Access, `AuthCta`. This job URL is SSR from Flask. The CTA block is: ```60:70:relocation_jobs/web/templates/job_posting.html
{{ primary_label }} {% if signed_in %} Continue to the official {{ company }} career page {% endif %} ...
``` `.jp-cta` is not a column. The orange button is `inline-flex`; the employer link is `inline-block`. On a wide screen they sit **on the same row**. `.jp-employer` also never turns off the underline, so it looks like a default browser hyperlink next to a designed button. That is why it feels like a different product from the rest of kuchup.com. “Open workspace” in the screenshot means you are signed in, which is the only case that paints this link. --- ### Why the Mollie link is there at all This page exists for the LinkedIn funnel, not the panel: 1. Crawler reads the JD + JSON-LD. 2. Apply lands on `https://kuchup.com/jobs/` (not Mollie). 3. Primary CTA is supposed to create/sign in and save the role into the company workspace. The docs for that funnel say the employer link is **never paywalled**: ```56:60:docs/reference/entitlements-and-opportunities.md Visa job pages at `GET /jobs/` are the LinkedIn/Google on-ramp. The primary CTA saves the role into looking-to-apply; the official employer link is never paywalled. | Plan | Unique `/jobs//save` | |------|----------------------------| | `free` | First **3** unique jobs per UTC day are free ... ``` The 3/day number only counts unique `/jobs//save` calls. `/jobs//employer` has no login check and no quota. It logs `employer_outbound` and 302s to the ATS: ```217:233:relocation_jobs/web/routes/job_pages.py @app.get("/jobs//employer") def public_job_employer(slug: str): ... resp = redirect(dest, code=302) ``` There is even a test that this stays uncapped after the three free saves (`test_employer_uncapped_after_daily_saves`). When the wallet is empty, the copy still says *“The official career page stays available above.”* So the current code is consistent with the syndication doc, and **inconsistent with the panel rule**. --- ### How this fights the policy you already have On the board / workspace, a free account is meant to stay inside Kuchup: - 10 matched companies - **3 roles per company** - 3 public saves per UTC day, then a credit - the rest of a company’s book is hidden (`jobs_hidden_count`) These `/jobs/` pages sit outside that. Every visa-positive catalog role gets a public URL with the **full JD**. Once you sign in, the ATS is one click away. You do not need a company slot, a remaining save, or a credit. That is the bypass: LinkedIn (or Google) → public job page → official career page, and Kuchup is optional. Anonymous visitors do **not** see the link in HTML. Anyone who hits `/jobs//employer` still gets the 302. The HTML hide is not the policy. --- ### What I would change (Ask mode — not applying it) Two different decisions: 1. **Layout** — easy. Make `.jp-cta` a column, style the employer link as muted secondary (no underline), or drop it from this page. 2. **Policy** — the real one. If the rule is “after 3 free jobs/day, use the panel, do not bounce to the employer,” then this page should not offer an ATS exit. Hide the link, and put auth + the same save quota on `/employer`. Show the real URL only after the role is in looking-to-apply, inside `/company/...`. I would **not** strip the JD from the public HTML. The wrapping funnel needs it for LinkedIn/Google. The leak is the outbound click, not the description. If you want this aligned with the panel wall, switch to Agent mode and we can remove the career-page exit from the interstitial and gate `/employer`.

input.plan:
# Close the public ATS bypass

Public job pages were built as a LinkedIn interstitial. They still show a signed-in **Continue to the official {employer} career page** link, and `GET /jobs/<slug>/employer` 302s to the ATS with no quota. That fights the rule: after 3 free public saves per day, stay in the panel.

Crawlers keep the full JD + JSON-LD (`applyUrl` already points at kuchup.com). Humans do not get an ATS bounce from this surface.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  LinkedIn[LinkedIn Apply] --> JobPage["GET /jobs/slug"]
  JobPage --> Save["GET /jobs/slug/save"]
  Save -->|3 free then credit| Workspace["/company/..."]
  Workspace --> ATS[Employer URL in workspace]
  EmployerOld["GET /jobs/slug/employer"] --> Save
```

## Product rule

- Public `/jobs/<slug>`: primary CTA only (track in Kuchup). No employer link.
- `/jobs/<slug>/employer`: never 302 to the ATS. Redirect to `/jobs/<slug>/save` (same Google OAuth `next=`, same 3/day + credit wall, same workspace landing).
- After looking-to-apply, the original posting stays on the company workspace (`companyApplyUrl` in [`relocation_jobs/static/js/company.js`](relocation_jobs/static/js/company.js)).
- Empty-wallet copy no longer says the career page is still available.

## Code

[`relocation_jobs/web/templates/job_posting.html`](relocation_jobs/web/templates/job_posting.html)

- Delete the `{% if signed_in %}` employer `<a>`.
- Change the `save_blocked` line from “The official career page stays available above” to the same pack / Full Access message without an ATS hint.

[`relocation_jobs/web/routes/job_pages.py`](relocation_jobs/web/routes/job_pages.py)

- Drop `employer_href` from `_job_page_context`.
- Change `public_job_employer` to `redirect` `/jobs/<slug>/save` (404 if the slug is unknown). Keep `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`. Drop `employer_outbound` ATS logging.

[`relocation_jobs/static/job-posting.css`](relocation_jobs/static/job-posting.css)

- Delete unused `.jp-employer`.

## Docs

- [`docs/reference/job-syndication.md`](docs/reference/job-syndication.md): interstitial has no secondary ATS link; `/employer` is a compatibility redirect into `/save`. Remove “tracked outbound to ATS” from the funnel diagram.
- [`docs/reference/entitlements-and-opportunities.md`](docs/reference/entitlements-and-opportunities.md): delete “the official employer link is never paywalled.” Public saves remain the quota; ATS URL is workspace-only.

## Tests

[`tests/web/test_job_pages.py`](tests/web/test_job_pages.py)

- Anonymous and signed-in job HTML: no “Continue to the official”, no `/employer` href.
- `GET /employer` (anon and signed-in): 302 to `/jobs/<slug>/save`, not the ATS URL.
- Replace `test_employer_uncapped_after_daily_saves`: after 3 free saves + empty wallet, `/employer` still must not 302 to the ATS (it follows `/save`, which stays on the paywall page).
- Keep existing save-quota tests as they are.

Run `pytest tests/web/test_job_pages.py -o addopts= -q --tb=line`.

## Out of scope

- Do not truncate the public JD (LinkedIn/Google still need it).
- Do not restyle the employer link; it goes away.
- Do not change board title links or workspace apply URL.
- Do not rebuild the Flask header to match the Next marketing nav.
